value.rationale: Three independent uniformly sampled points on a fixed hyperbolic circumcircle define a canonical curvature-sensitive shape statistic, unlike arbitrary angle-coordinate measures. The closed dilogarithmic law gives a complete exact probability profile for all positive radii, uniquely reconstructs radius from one geometric frequency, and quantifies both the Euclidean small-circle regime and the ideal-triangle limit with explicit nontrivial logarithmically enhanced exponential tail. The probability is not a renamed known constant or an arbitrarily narrow computation.
